solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bob, or who got him pass to see air display?

definitions.meaning: the name Bob reads the same backwards and forwards, a classic example of a word with that property

definitions.text: who got him pass to see air display?
definitions.meaning: a friend who got him a pass to an air show is a pal in the aerodrome

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: break the answer into PAL + IN + DROME, a mate who wangled him a pass and is now inside the (aero)drome watching the display.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob is a textbook example of a word spelt the same either way round, which is the defining property.

clue.text: On return, continue to see

indicators.note: on return means the word for continue is read the other way round, from bottom to top in this down light

parts.note: to keep on is to continue, so keep means continue

explanation.surface: Someone coming back carries on, so as to look at something.
explanation.definitionFit: To peek is to take a quick look, so it is a loose synonym for see.

clue.text: Scot who touched down in the valley?

definitions.meaning: someone from the southern, lowland part of Scotland, as opposed to a Highlander

definitions.text: who touched down in the valley?
definitions.meaning: one who landed low down, in a valley

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into LOW + LANDER, someone who touched down in low ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lowlander is a native of the Scottish Lowlands, the southern and central part of Scotland, so a kind of Scot.

clue.text: At least eighteen pennies change, to end with

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the remaining letters into a new order
to end with means only the closing letters of pennies are used, dropping its opening pair

explanation.surface: A sum of at least eighteen pennies is changed into other coins, to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to end with' keeps the last five letters of 'pennies', NNIES, which 'change' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural means two or more nines, and two nines add up to eighteen, the smallest total possible.

clue.text: Unseasoned wood? That's not fair

parts.note: raw means unseasoned, as timber not yet dried or food not yet flavoured
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A carpenter complains that the timber supplied has not been dried properly.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL is the British word for softwood planks of pine or fir.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting unfair or harsh treatment is the idiomatic meaning of the phrase, as in 'that's a raw deal'.

clue.text: They get embroiled in things

definitions.meaning: read as things that mat, that is become tangled or matted together
affairs or subjects, as in 'these things take time'

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading treats the word as 'mat-ters', items that mat or tangle up; the second is the everyday sense of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means affairs or topics, a straight synonym for things in the general sense.

clue.text: Almost lower a boat

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to lower (or lour) is to frown, so it means scowl

explanation.surface: Instructions to bring a boat down nearly all the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' is not the opposite of raise here but the verb rhyming with 'flower', meaning to frown.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat used for carrying freight, so an example of a boat.

clue.text: Tea imbibed at home with mate

indicators.note: imbibed means taken in, so the word for at home is drunk inside the word for tea

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Having a cup of tea at home with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, 'china plate' rhymes with 'mate', so a china is a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang shortens 'china plate' to its first word, giving a familiar word for a friend or pal.

clue.text: How surprising! Listed as wealthy

parts.note: 'well!' is an exclamation of surprise
a ship that lists leans to one side, which is also called heeling

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed to find a person's name on the rich list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listed' looks like 'put on a list' but is the nautical sense of leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone rich or comfortably off, so it is a synonym for wealthy.

clue.text: Man cleaned windows on the inside

indicators.note: on the inside means the letters sit within the words cleaned windows, spanning both

explanation.surface: A fellow washed the windows from inside the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin is a male first name, so the man is an example of someone called by it.

clue.text: Cheerfully, having left one's affairs in order

definitions.meaning: doing a job eagerly and with energy

definitions.text: having left one's affairs in order
definitions.meaning: literally possessing a will, a legal document saying how your estate is to be divided

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for doing something with gusto is read literally as owning a testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means energetically and willingly, close to cheerfully; literally it means possessing a testament for one's estate.

clue.text: Put on trial, as a rule, for speaking out

indicators.note: for speaking out says the words are pronounced, giving a word that sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule by a monarch

explanation.surface: Bringing a person to court is, generally, a matter of speaking up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a rule' looks like the phrase 'usually', but 'as' is a link and 'a rule' is A REIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign someone is to bring them before a court to answer a criminal charge.

clue.text: Better half has a purpose for screen: that's plain

indicators.note: the word for purpose acts as a screen, enclosing the letters taken from better

parts.note: use means purpose or function, as in 'what's the use?'

indicators.note: half points to three of the six letters of better, here its back half

explanation.surface: A wife is said to need a screen for some reason, and that is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better half' looks like a spouse, but it means half the letters of 'better'; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severely simple and without decoration, so it is a synonym for plain.

clue.text: Removing head, open up fish

indicators.note: removing head means the opening letter of the word is taken off

parts.note: to broach a cask or a subject is to open it up

explanation.surface: Instructions for gutting a fish: cut the head off and slit it open.
explanation.definitionFit: The roach is a freshwater fish of the carp family, so an example of a fish.

clue.text: Keeping quiet while clinching a deal

definitions.meaning: 'wrap up!' is British slang for 'be quiet!'
bringing a negotiation to a successful close, finishing it off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap up' as an order to shut up is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both concluding a business agreement and, in British slang, shutting up.

clue.text: Cardinal point missing, requiring change that's fundamental

indicators.note: requiring change says the remaining letters must be rearranged
missing means the compass letter is left out of the word cardinal

parts.note: N is north, one of the cardinal points of the compass

explanation.surface: A cardinal compass point is gone, so the change needed is a radical one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops the N from CARDINAL to give CARDIAL, and 'requiring change' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical change goes to the root of things, so radical is a synonym for fundamental.

clue.text: Who made us react strangely, in other words

indicators.note: strangely means the letters of react are set in an odd new order

parts.note: or introduces an alternative phrasing, meaning 'in other words'

explanation.surface: A question about how our maker might respond oddly, put another way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Creator is God, the being believed to have made humankind.

clue.text: After second drink, produce work that's spotty

indicators.note: after means the drink comes following the abbreviation for second

parts.note: a tipple is an alcoholic drink, and to tipple is to drink

explanation.surface: Having a second drink, someone turns out sloppy work.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipple is to paint or draw using small dots, producing a speckled or dotted effect.

clue.text: Small audience watching 'Home For the Homeless'

parts.note: a small turnout is described as poor
a house is the audience in a theatre, as in 'a full house'

explanation.surface: Few people turn up to watch a play or programme called 'Home For the Homeless'.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends 'Home For the Homeless' is a show title in quotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A poorhouse was an institution where paupers with nowhere else to live were housed.

clue.text: Nobody rich in France

parts.note: a French-derived word for a nobody who has suddenly become rich, an upstart

explanation.walkthrough: The word is French (literally 'arrived'), which is what 'in France' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, from French, describes a person of humble origins who has newly gained wealth, an upstart or nobody made rich.

clue.text: Very Scottish — South not so boorish

parts.note: unco is a Scottish word meaning very

indicators.note: not means the letters of so are taken away from the word south

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scot remarks that people in the south are not very rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not so' removes the letters S and O from SOUTH, leaving UTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncouth means lacking good manners or refinement, a synonym of boorish.

clue.text: Forgive cheat that's cheated

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat them
to be done is to be cheated, as in 'I've been done'

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to pardon a swindler who has been swindled in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone a wrong is to overlook or pardon it, a near synonym for forgive.

clue.text: Understand the safe way to carry firearm

definitions.meaning: to grasp an idea, to twig

definitions.text: the safe way to carry firearm
definitions.meaning: with the safety catch engaged, so the weapon cannot fire

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the words literally: a gun is safest with its safety catch on.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to grasp or twig something; read literally, it describes a gun with its safety engaged.

clue.text: Sending back, write within 'Article unskilled'

indicators.note: within means the reversed word for write sits inside the word for article

parts.note: it is a pronoun standing for an unspecified article or thing

indicators.note: sending back means the word for write is turned round

parts.note: to pen a letter is to write it

explanation.surface: A clumsy article is being returned, written up as no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' is not 'a' or 'the' here but an object, which the pronoun IT stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill or competence, a direct synonym of unskilled.

clue.text: From painting, stands to make more

parts.note: ex is Latin for from, as in 'ex works'

indicators.note: stands means the word for painting is set upright, read upwards in this down light

parts.note: painting is an example of art

explanation.surface: Someone takes stands away from a painting exhibition to make more room.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, so it is a synonym of more as in 'a little more'.

clue.text: Mermaid's pet?

parts.note: a mermaid, living underwater, would keep a sea creature as a pet in place of a cat

explanation.walkthrough: A land-dweller keeps a cat; a mermaid's cat would be a fish version of it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a real fish with whisker-like barbels; the clue jokingly imagines it as an undersea household pet.

clue.text: Family is sure right away

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is taken out of the word sure

explanation.surface: A relative is certain straight off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately' but splits into R and a deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal and formal word for offspring or descendants, so one's children or family.

clue.text: Sees what put an end to Pompeii, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak says the letters are spoken out, giving a word that is pronounced the same

parts.words: what put an end to Pompeii
parts.note: the last two letters of the name Pompeii are two Is, or I's

explanation.surface: Someone is curious about what destroyed the Roman town of Pompeii.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put an end to Pompeii' looks like Vesuvius, but it is the two I's at the end of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it, so the verb form is a synonym of sees.

clue.text: Experience, as you look at each in turn

definitions.meaning: to undergo or endure something, as in 'what she had to suffer'

definitions.text: as you look at each in turn
definitions.meaning: examining items one by one, as in checking papers

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one phrasal verb: undergoing an ordeal and working through a pile of things.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both enduring something and examining a set of items one after another.

clue.text: Painting a room

definitions.meaning: a preliminary sketch or picture made as practice for a larger work
a room in a house used for reading and writing

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated nouns: an artist's practice piece and a room for work.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's sketch for a larger work and a home's book-lined workroom both take this name.

clue.text: I vetoed unattractive design

indicators.note: vetoed means the letter I is rejected and thrown out of the word

parts.note: plain means unattractive, as of a person's looks

explanation.surface: Someone refused an ugly proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I vetoed' looks like the speaker objecting; instead the letter I is barred from PLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme or drawing for how something is to be made, synonymous with design.

clue.text: Always the same — lacking the means for a tip

parts.note: loose coins are what you use to tip a waiter
less means without, as in 'penniless'

explanation.surface: A diner lacks small coins for a gratuity, the same old story.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word as CHANGE-LESS: having no coins to tip with.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never alters is unvarying, constant, forever unaltered.
